liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Iko Iko** (4 reviews): Considered the best Iko ever, better than Rochester; after it the listener felt the band could leave the stage satisfied; Dense, demanding Iko with sound coming from all directions; close to the reviewer's favorite [19][21][25][26]
- **Dear Mr. Fantasy** (4 reviews): Dear Mr. Fantasy called epic; Dear Mr. Fantasy judged mediocre, with better versions on 7/4/87 at Foxboro or in Portland, ME [20][22][27][29]
- **Shakedown Street** (2 reviews): Shakedown Street lacks snap, which for this reviewer makes the show nearly unlistenable; Funky, groovy Shakedown Street, not a speed version [24][25]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): Garcia's voice was left raspy, like Kermit the Frog, on his small parts in Cassidy [21]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Serious Minglewood; Garcia's second solo takes a big turn with wicked runs [25]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Jack Straw was played with full intensity, leaving nothing held back [21]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Good Not Fade Away but not the best [22]
- **U.S. Blues** (1 review): U.S. Blues was strong, played on Flag Day [19]
- The Playin' space is included within the Playin' In The Band Reprise track [5]

## Setlist highlights

- **drums // drums**: rare: 4 archived performances [30]
- **crowd NFA chant**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 9 archived performances [30]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-06-14.148196.beyerm88.holbrook.flac2448** (recommended): source not stated; 18 songs; 125 min [1]
- **gd84-06-14.sbd.hinko.18804.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 132 min; rated 4/5 by 16 [3]. Said about its sound: Describes the soundboard as a great board; Says Red Rocks' thin air makes soundboards run wide open and sound like a transistor radio; audience tapes are thin [18][27]
- **gd1984-06-14.167060.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 17 songs; 126 min [5]
- **gd1984-06-14.nakcm304-mikeg-suraci.suraci.78371.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 17 songs; 122 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended; says the second set was excellent [20]
- Bobby remarks that on this date in 1877 the American flag was adopted [1]
- Second set is judged weaker in performance than its setlist suggests on paper [18]
- Iko Iko rated better than the Rochester version [19]
- Only a better Iko Iko the reviewer knows is from 6-24-85; a St. Stephen tease precedes Not Fade Away [20]
- Considered a fun show but not on the level of Princeton [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-06-14.148196.beyerm88.holbrook.flac2448**: taped by Executive Crew Tom Pinney, Sean Murtha, Chris Kidwell, Kyle Holbrook; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: MAUD CA: Beyer M88 cardiod XY > Sony TCD5M|maxell MX90 x2 no NR Location: 80 feet from stage DFC [1]. Also: Recording is missing the first few seconds after a tape flip [1]
- **gd84-06-14.sbd.hinko.18804.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > MC > C > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN [3]. Also: Soundboard transferred through MC, cassette, DAT and CD, then EAC to SHN by Darryl Hinko [3]
- **gd1984-06-14.167060.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME-80 mics > Sony D5M [5]. Also: A Schoeps source from the Oade's patches 0:16 in the Jack Straw transition and 0:34 in Drums [5]
- **gd1984-06-14.nakcm304-mikeg-suraci.suraci.78371.flac16**: taped by Tony Suraci and Mike G; transferred by Tony Suraci; source: *Nak CM304's>Sony D5M>Sony D5M(XLIIS) At SBD#, Stand at 7 feet. [7]. Also: Recorded with Mike G.'s mics, plugged into his D5, directly behind the board at Red Rocks [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Concertposterauction.com: [Grateful Dead Red Rocks Amphitheatre 1984 Silkscreen Concert Poster](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/1204852/Grateful-Dead-Red-Rocks-Amphitheatre-1984-Silkscreen-Concert-Poster) [31]
- Poster by Steven Rood Grateful Dead: [1984-06-14 Red Rocks Amphitheatre, Morrison, CO, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1984-06-14-red-rocks-amphitheatre-morrison-co-usa/) [32]
